verdict: Avoid new jute-mill exposure in Howrah; lend only to value-added jute product converters with proven non-MSP order books, and then only on tight structured terms.
title: Howrah Jute Mills & Products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A Howrah jute mill buys raw jute, spins and weaves it into sacking, hessian and yarn, and sells largely into government MSP procurement plus some export and value-added trade. **Cash is made in the spread between raw jute cost and finished goods price, and that spread is thin and cyclical.** Working capital is seasonal and swings with the market price of raw jute versus its MSP [8][10]. Capex is heavy and lumpy; the rating methodology flags weaving as fixed- and working-capital intensive with high funding needs [11]. So when a proposal lands, check the raw-jute-to-finished-goods spread and the order book mix; if the buyer list is mostly MSP, ask what share is genuinely non-MSP and priced independently. ## What has broken now
Howrah is closing mills, not opening them. West Bengal's own signals are weak: GST collections -1.3% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D], and electricity demand +5.7% versus India +9.5% [D]. India-wide exports are -13.6% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. ## Where the growth is
Peer rating work points the other way from the mills: Crisil expects jute sales volumes up 15% with a twenty percent rise in domestic demand, helped by lower raw jute prices and value-added products [6][7]. **Pursue converters and value-added jute product makers with diversified buyers, not commodity sacking mills.** Avoid single-mill sacking spinners with MSP-dependent order books and no modernisation record [2]. Note the local project tracker shows textiles/yarn projects in Bengal [1] but says nothing specific to Howrah jute; collect from customer any city-level pipeline. ## How to grow safely
Structure as short-tenor working capital against confirmed orders, not term debt for mill modernisation. **Take stock and book-debt statements monthly, and raw jute price versus MSP every month** [8][10]. Covenant a minimum non-MSP order share and a debt-service cover floor; if the customer cannot produce audited spread data, collect from customer before sanction. ## Early-warning signs
- Monthly stock statement (monthly): inventory ageing beyond 90 days -> freeze fresh limits. - Monthly GST returns (monthly): filing gaps or falling turnover -> reduce exposure. - Quarterly wages/PF (quarterly): delayed statutory payments -> treat as closure risk [2]. - Monthly power bill (monthly): falling units consumed -> verify running hours before renewal.
